items.q: A 63‑year‑old male presents with groin pain 4 months after a cemented total hip arthroplasty. Radiographs show a radiolucent line at the bone‑cement interface but no subsidence of the femoral stem. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
items.e: A radiolucent line at the bone‑cement interface without subsidence is classic for aseptic loosening.

items.q: Which sterilisation method for polyethylene does NOT generate free radicals that require subsequent antioxidant treatment?
items.e: Gamma irradiation in nitrogen does not produce free radicals, unlike the other methods.

items.q: A 45‑year‑old woman with osteonecrosis of the femoral head is scheduled for a femoral head replacement. Which implant material should be avoided as a femoral head bearing surface because of poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity?
items.e: Titanium alloy has poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity, making it unsuitable as a head bearing surface.

items.q: A 70‑year‑old man develops a loud audible squeak during gait 3 years after a ceramic‑on‑ceramic total hip replacement. Which surgical parameter is most strongly correlated with this complication?
o: Incomplete seating of the polyethylene liner
28 mm ceramic head instead of 36 mm
items.e: Squeaking in ceramic‑on‑ceramic bearings is most strongly associated with steep cup inclination (> 50°) causing edge loading.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) manufactured by remelting?
items.e: Remelting reduces free radicals but does not increase wear resistance; it may reduce fracture toughness.

items.q: A 52‑year‑old patient with a history of long lumbar fusion now presents with low back pain and hip instability. The most important spinopelvic consideration after the fusion is that the pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly, thereby reducing functional cup anteversion. This statement reflects the fact that the pelvis:
o: Loses its ability to tilt in all directions
items.e: After a long lumbar fusion the pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly, which reduces functional cup anteversion and increases dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following materials shows almost no plastic deformation before failure, i.e., is classified as brittle?
items.e: Ceramics such as bone exhibit brittle behaviour, with little plastic deformation before failure.

items.q: Which of the following is the most common metal sensitiser in the general population?
items.e: The most common metal sensitiser in the general population is nickel.

items.q: Which alloying element in cobalt‑chromium‑molybdenum alloys primarily forms a passive oxide layer that resists corrosion?
items.e: Chromium forms a passive chromium oxide layer that improves corrosion resistance.

items.q: In a cemented femoral stem, the third‑generation cementing technique involves all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Use of a distal canal plug
Vacuum mixing to reduce porosity and improve centralisation
items.e: Third‑generation cementing uses vacuum mixing and centralisers; retrograde cement gun insertion is not a feature of this technique.

items.q: In a 24‑year‑old male who sustained a midshaft femoral fracture, the surgeon chooses a titanium interlocking nail. Upon reaming, the surgeon notices a thin, lamellated cortical layer on the medullary canal. Which property of titanium alloys makes them unsuitable as a femoral head bearing surface, as stated in the source text?
o: Poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity
items.e: Titanium alloy is unsuitable as a femoral head bearing mainly because of poor wear (abrasion) resistance and notch sensitivity.

items.q: A patient is being prepared for a total knee arthroplasty. The target tibial polyethylene thickness should be at least what measurement, according to the source?
items.e: The minimum recommended tibial polyethylene thickness in TKA is about 8 mm.

items.q: A 68‑year‑old woman with a history of long‑term steroid use wants a hip arthroplasty. Which metal sensitiser is most common in the general population, as per the source?
items.e: The most common metal sensitiser in the general population is Nickel.

items.q: During the direct anterior hip approach, which vessel is routinely ligated to prevent bleeding?
o: Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral vessels
items.e: In the direct anterior approach the ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral vessels is typically ligated.

items.q: A 71‑year‑old man has a long lumbar fusion and now needs a THA. Which biomechanical concept explains his increased dislocation risk?
o: The pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly on sitting, reducing functional cup anteversion
items.e: A long lumbar fusion limits posterior pelvic tilt on sitting, decreasing functional cup anteversion and increasing dislocation risk.

items.q: What is the primary decelerative factor that a femoral head fracture revision should avoid, as listed in the source?
o: Using a ceramic head directly on a mildly damaged trunnion
Using a ceramic head with a titanium adapter sleeve
Applying bone cement on the taper
items.e: When the trunnion is mildly damaged, a ceramic head should not be used directly; a metal head is recommended.

items.q: A patient develops a periprosthetic joint infection. Which investigation measures free radicals associated with polyethylene oxidation and thus is NOT suitable for sterilisation of polyethylene?
items.e: Gamma irradiation in air generates free radicals; nitrogen reduces them.

items.q: During a direct lateral approach, excessive splitting of which muscle increases the risk of superior gluteal nerve injury?
o: Gluteus medius more than 10 cm above the tip of the greater trochanter
Gluteus medius more than 1 cm above the tip
Gluteus medius more than 5 cm above the tip
At the level of the lesser trochanter
items.e: Splitting gluteus medius more than 10 cm above the greater trochanter risks the superior gluteal nerve.

items.q: What is the approximate elastic modulus of a cobalt‑chromium‑molybdenum alloy relative to titanium, as inferred from the source?
items.e: Cobalt‑chromium alloys have a higher elastic modulus compared to titanium alloys.

items.q: Which of the following statements about bone cement is FALSE according to the source?
o: Cement setting time is shortened by increased ambient temperature
Barium sulphate is a radiopacifier in commercial cement
Nerve injury is the most common complication of cementation
items.e: The source does not state nerve injury as a common complication; cement is strongest in compression, setting time shortened by temperature and barium sulphate is a radiopacifier.

items.q: In a patient who has received a ceramic head after a head fracture, what is the recommended bearing for revision?
o: Ceramic head with sleeve and synovectomy
items.e: Revision after ceramic head fracture should use a ceramic head (with sleeve) and thorough synovectomy.

items.q: Which type of wear particle from metal-on-metal bearings is most clinically relevant, per the source?
items.e: Metal‑on‑metal wear particles are typically nanometre‑sized (about 10‑50 nm).

items.q: A 55‑year‑old male had a total knee arthroplasty with a proximally fixed, distally cemented femoral stem. What is the most common mechanism of fatigue fracture of a cemented femoral stem?
o: Proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem (cantilever bending)
items.e: The classic fatigue fracture mechanism is proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem, acting as a cantilever.

items.q: A 62‑year‑old male presents with a femoral shaft fracture 4 weeks post–cemented THA; radiographs show a short diaphyseal fragment adjacent to a well‑fixed femoral stem. According to the Vancouver classification, this fracture is best managed with:
o: Excision of the fragment and revision with a long uncemented stem
Open reduction with plate and cables without stem revision
items.e: Vancouver Type B1 – fracture around a well‑fixed stem; treatment is ORIF with plates and cables.

items.q: The ‘L’ in 316L stainless steel used for orthopedic implants denotes:
items.e: 316L refers to low carbon content, reducing notch sensitivity.

items.q: Which metal combination is MOST prone to galvanic corrosion in the joint space?
items.e: Titanium alloy in contact with cobalt–chromium forms the most severe galvanic couple.

items.q: During a direct lateral (Hardinge) approach, a split of gluteus medius more than 1 cm above the tip of the greater trochanter most endangers which nerve?
items.e: The superior gluteal nerve runs near the gluteus medius insertion and can be injured if the split is high.

items.q: What is the threshold joint reaction force across the hip in single‑leg stance?
items.e: Typical joint load is 2.5–3 times body weight in single‑leg stance.

items.q: The most common reason for proximal femoral fractures in revision THA with a long femoral stem is:
o: Proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem (cantilever bending)
items.e: Stem failure in revision is often due to cantilever bending of a well‑fixed distal stem.

items.q: Which shoulder or ankle implant surface coating aims for a porous thickness of 50–75 µm to promote osseointegration?
items.e: Hydroxyapatite coatings are optimally 50–75 µm for bone ongrowth.

items.q: The ‘effective joint space’ concept explains:
o: Wear particle dissemination via synovial fluid
items.e: It describes how wear particles travel distant from their origin through joint fluid.

items.q: In a total knee arthroplasty, increasing tibiofemoral conformity:
o: Decreases contact stress but increases fixation interface stress
items.e: Higher conformity reduces load per area but transfers more stress to fixation surfaces.

items.q: Which of the following is a major diagnostic criterion for periprosthetic joint infection according to the 2018 MSIS/ICM criteria?
o: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis
items.e: A sinus tract is one of the two major criteria for PJI.

items.q: The 80° cup inclination and 20° anteversion Lewinnek "safe zone" for acetabular components is:
items.e: Lewinnek’s safe zone is 55±5° inclination and 25±5° anteversion.

items.q: A ceramic head placed on a mildly damaged trunnion is best used with:
o: A ceramic head with a titanium adapter sleeve
items.e: Use a ceramic head with a titanium sleeve to avoid sharpening wear on a damaged trunnion.

items.q: Which statement about highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) is FALSE?
o: It is produced by gamma irradiation in nitrogen
Free radicals generated during irradiation are scavenged by vitamin E
Remelting eliminates free radicals but reduces fatigue strength
It is cross‑linked by electron beam alone
items.e: Remelting does not eliminate free radicals; it reduces fatigue strength and toughness.

items.q: Two‑spot chondrosarcoma in the distal femur is most commonly classified under which objective tissue type?
items.e: Chondrosarcomas arise from cartilaginous tissue.

items.q: A patient with a long lumbar fusion has higher THA dislocation risk mainly because:
o: The pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly on sitting, reducing functional cup anteversion
items.e: Fixed pelvis limits posterior tilt, decreasing functional cup anteversion and raising dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following describes the failure mode of backside wear between a polyethylene liner and the metal acetabular shell?
items.e: Backside wear corresponds to Mode 4 wear.

items.q: A 68‑year‑old female presents with chronic groin pain and a prominent anterior acetabular rim on her post‑operative X‑ray. She had a primary total hip arthroplasty 10 years ago. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
items.e: A prominent anterior cup edge leads to iliopsoas impingement, a frequent cause of groin pain after THA.

items.q: During templating for a revision of a femoral stem with a well‑fixed distal tip, the surgeon plans a distal‑seam‑cutoplasty. For such a stem, which property of the cement mantle is most critical?
o: No cement washout at the tip
items.e: Cement mantle thickness of 4–6 mm is the accepted optimum; a thinner mantle leads to higher risk of stem pull‑out.

items.q: A 55‑year‑old man with a planar fracture of the intertrochanteric region is managed with a short cephalomedullary nail. Which bone‑plugged design advantage is unique to such nails?
items.e: The short head‑neck shaft plug enhances rotational stability of intertrochanteric fractures fixed with short nails.

items.q: Which of the following statements about highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) is correct?
o: It has a higher modulus than conventional PE
It is more oxidised after remelting
Free radicals are scavenged by Vitamin E
It is produced by heat treatment only
items.e: Vitamin E is added to HXLPE to scavenge free radicals and reduce oxidation without compromising cross‑link density.

items.q: All of the following are true regarding the ‘epiphyseal marker’ in paediatric arthroplasty except:
o: It is used in hips with developmental dysplasia of the hip
It is a fixed cortical ridge
It is located at the acetabulum
It cannot be used after growth arrest
items.e: The epiphyseal marker is a cortical ridge within the femoral neck, not at the acetabulum.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised mode of third‑body wear in joint arthroplasty?
o: Bone fragments trapped at the cartilage/metal interface
items.e: Third‑body wear originates from bone, osteophytes or particulate debris, not from surgical gloves.

items.q: A 62‑year‑old woman develops unexplained swelling around the hip and elevated ESR after a primary THA. The surgeon suspects a prosthetic joint infection. Which investigation is most definitive for this diagnosis?
items.e: Joint aspiration with culture is the gold standard for diagnosing periprosthetic joint infection.

items.q: The most common normal‑world metal sensitiser among orthopaedic implant patients is:
items.e: Nickel is the most common metal sensitiser in the general population, including orthopaedic patients.

items.q: In the case of a patient with a long lumbar fusion, the risk of dislocation after a primary THA is primarily due to:
o: Insufficient functional cup anteversion from limited pelvic tilt
items.e: A fused lumbar spine limits posterior pelvic tilt, reducing functional cup anteversion and increasing dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following is the main biomechanical disadvantage of a rotating‑hinge knee prosthesis compared to a CCK insert in revision TKA?
o: Increased lever‑arm shear forces to the bone‑implant interface
Higher incidence of patellar tendon rupture
items.e: Rotating‑hinge implants transfer excess shear stresses across the bone–implant interface, increasing loosening risk.

items.q: A 73‑year‑old man with a revised total knee arthroplasty receives a polyethylene insert with a 6 mm thickness. This thickness is:
o: Excessive with risk of implant failure
The exact optimal thickness for all knees
items.e: The minimum recommended tibial polyethylene thickness in TKA is about 6 mm.

items.q: Which of the following best describes the brake‑like stabilisation offered by the ‘laryngopsoas’ muscle in a total hip arthroplasty?
o: It provides a discontinuous bony fixation
It stabilises the joint in extension only
items.e: The psoas‑iliopsoas tendon complex limits internal rotation, acting as a brake on the hip joint.

items.q: The system of Wasielewski acetabular quadrants is used to identify screws that may injure:
items.e: Screws in the anterosuperior quadrant of the acetabulum are close to the obturator nerve and vessels.

items.q: During an emergency CT of a 70‑year‑old woman who fell from standing height, a wedge fracture of L5 is seen with the anterior height reduced by 35% and a hypertrophic fragment of the posterior wall. The sagittal alignment of the adjacent vertebrae is normal. Which of the following best describes the fracture according to the AO Spine Thoracolumbar Injury Classification System?
o: AO A1 – Compression with no posterior wall involvement
items.e: The fracture is a pure compression type ‑ an A3 in the AO system. The posterior wall fragment represents a small bony fragment; the sagittal alignment is maintained, and there is no spinal cord involvement.

items.q: A 30‑year‑old construction worker presents with progressive thoracic back pain for 6 weeks. MRI shows a bony fragment eroding the posterior elements of T8 and an associated epidural hematoma causing mild spinal cord compression. What is the most urgent investigative step?
o: Immediate CT angiography of the aneurysm
CT of the thoracolumbar spine with 3‑D reconstruction
items.e: The magnetic resonance sequence reveals a bony fragment compressing the cord with an epidural hematoma. Rapid surgical decompression is indicated to prevent permanent neurological deficit.

items.q: A 12‑year‑old child falls from a 2‑metre height and sustains a T10 burst fracture. Plain radiographs show a wedge deformity with no dislocation. The neurological exam is normal. According to the Denis three‑column model, which column is most likely intact?
items.e: In a burst fracture, the middle (vertebral body/annulus) column is compromised, while anterior and posterior columns remain intact. Consequently, the posterior facet and ligaments are usually preserved.

items.q: The risk of neurological compromise in a thoracolumbar burst fracture can be best predicted by which radiographic parameter?
o: Degree of canal encroachment >50 % of the sagittal diameter
items.e: Severe canal encroachment (>50 % of the sagittal diameter) correlates strongly with spinal cord injury risk, whereas height loss, facet displacement, and kyphosis alone are less predictive.

items.q: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a right flank abdominal pain after a motorcycle crash. CT demonstrates an isolated L3 burst fracture with a pars fracture and a small inferior facet fracture, but the neurological exam is intact. The TLICS score is:
items.e: The fracture is a type B (bifragmentary‑pars) with a posterior element injury; combined loss of alignment and minimal neurological deficit gives a TLICS of 6, indicating surgery. (The 6 is obtained from 3 points for the fracture type plus 2 for minor neurological deficit and 1 for injury severity).

items.q: During a staged fixation of a thoracolumbar fracture–dislocation, which intra‑operative adjunct is most reliable for confirming the quality of the pedicle screw purchase?
o: Pin pull testing with a calibrated force gauge
items.e: Pin pull testing with a calibrated gauge directly measures screw‑bone pullout strength, offering real‑time confirmation of purchase.

items.q: In a pediatric patient with a T12–L1 burst fracture, the appropriate revision strategy after an initial rigid halo vest immobilization that resulted in persistent pain is:
o: Exchange the halo for an external fixator
Add a posterior pedicle screw construct
Revise the halo with additional head pins
items.e: The most effective approach is to add a posterior pedicle screw construct to stabilize the fracture, especially when pain persists with external fixation alone.

items.q: A 28‑year‑old male sustains a high‑velocity motorcycle crash and develops sudden back pain. Plain radiographs show a burst fracture of T12 with a comminuted posterior wall fragment. Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the management of this fracture?
o: Posterior pedicle screw fixation alone provides adequate stability because the posterior elements bear most of the load
An anterior corpectomy with titanium cage and plating is mandatory to restore height and anterior column support
Minimally invasive percutaneous pedicle screw fixation with bed rest for 12 weeks is sufficient
Combined anterior‑posterior instrumentation is preferable if kyphosis exceeds 30°
items.e: In a burst fracture with >30° kyphosis, combined anterior‑posterior fixation best restores alignment and prevents progressive deformity.

items.q: A 52‑year‑old woman falls onto a rolled mattress and presents with lower limb weakness and urinary incontinence. MRI shows a subarachnoid hematoma at L1‑L2 with a 10‑mm epidural bony fragment compressing the spinal cord. According to the Thoracolumbar Injury Classification and Severity Score (TLICS), what is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Anterior decompression with corpectomy and fusion
Posterior pedicle screw fixation with decompression and fusion
items.e: A burst fracture with neurological deficit scores 8 (4 for column injury + 3 for neurologic + 1 for displacement) mandates surgical treatment; posterior pedicle fixation with decompression is the recommended approach.

items.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a hanging‑type thoracolumbar fracture‑dislocation?
o: Transverse fracture line across the vertebral body
Displacement of the superior fragment posteriorly over the pedicle
Lateral shift of the entire vertebral body
Alar facet fracture with no involvement of the pedicle
items.e: In a hanging‑type fracture‑dislocation, the superior fragment drapes posteriorly over the pedicle, creating a 'flap‑leg' appearance.

items.q: The most reliable single imaging finding that predicts non‑union in a displaced thoracolumbar burst fracture is:
o: Presence of a posterior wall fragment larger than 5 mm
A canal compromise of >50% on CT
Deformity of the pedicle on AP view
items.e: A posterior wall fragment >5 mm indicates incomplete healing potential and correlates strongly with non‑union.

items.q: A 35‑year‑old office worker develops chronic lower back pain after a lumbar MRI shows a grade 1 spondylolisthesis at L4‑L5. Which of the following is NOT a contraindication for a minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS‑TLIF) at this level?
o: Spinal canal stenosis with >30 % diameter reduction
Presence of a well‑demarcated disc herniation at L4‑L5
items.e: A well‑demarcated disc herniation is actually an indication for TLIF, not a contraindication.

items.q: During a retrospective review, surgeons noted that patients undergoing posterior short‑segment fixation for T12‑L1 burst fractures had a higher incidence of cement‑augmented pedicle screws if they had:
items.e: Low BMD (T‑score <−2.0) increases screw loosening; cement augmentation mitigates this risk.

items.q: In a thoracolumbar fracture with an ISCORE of 3 (low), the recommended initial management is:
o: Halo‑vest traction for 3 weeks followed by surgery
Conservative treatment with bracing and close imaging follow‑up
items.e: An ISCORE of 3 indicates a stable injury; conservative management with bracing and serial imaging is the standard approach.

items.q: A 60‑year‑old male presents with chronic back pain after a fall from 3 m. The CT shows a vertebral body comminution at L2‑L3 with a posterior wall fragment of 18 mm. Which of the following statements best describes the risk of future kyphotic deformity?
o: It is low because the posterior wall fragment will heal spontaneously
The risk is significant if the fragment is >15 mm and the anterior height loss is >20 %
Kyphosis develops only if the facet joints are injured
The presence of a disc herniation above the fracture protects against deformity
items.e: A posterior fragment >15 mm and >20 % anterior height loss predict progressive kyphosis in thoracolumbar fractures.

items.q: A 64-year-old diabetic has 6 weeks of worsening low back pain, night pain and a raised CRP. Plain radiographs are normal. Which imaging investigation is most sensitive and specific for early pyogenic spondylodiscitis?
items.e: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI is the investigation of choice: disc and end-plate T2 hyperintensity, marrow oedema and enhancement appear within days, long before radiographic change, and it also shows epidural or paravertebral abscess.

items.q: Twelve months after an instrumented posterolateral L4–S1 fusion, a patient has persistent back pain and pseudarthrosis is suspected. Which is the most accurate non-invasive investigation to assess the fusion?
o: Fine-cut CT with sagittal and coronal reconstructions
items.e: Thin-slice CT with multiplanar reconstruction best shows continuous trabecular bridging or a pseudarthrosis cleft and screw lucency; flexion–extension films are insensitive across rigid instrumentation and MRI is degraded by metal artefact.

items.q: A 66-year-old with a previous L2–S1 instrumented fusion is planned for THA. On standing and sitting lateral spinopelvic radiographs, which finding best identifies a 'stiff' spinopelvic unit with a higher risk of dislocation?
o: Change in sacral slope of less than 10° between standing and sitting
items.e: Normally the pelvis tilts posteriorly on sitting and sacral slope falls by about 20° or more; a change below 10° indicates a stiff spinopelvic unit, which increases impingement and instability after THA and favours dual-mobility or adjusted cup positioning.

items.q: A 9-year-old has a closed, isolated, minimally displaced transverse midshaft tibial fracture with an intact fibula after a fall. Soft tissues and neurovascular status are normal. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Closed reduction if needed and an above-knee cast
items.e: Most closed paediatric tibial shaft fractures heal well with closed treatment in a long-leg cast; because an intact fibula tends to make the tibia drift into varus, alignment is checked with serial radiographs in the first weeks.

items.q: After closed reduction and percutaneous pinning of a Gartland III extension supracondylar humerus fracture in a 6-year-old, the radial pulse is not palpable but the hand is warm and pink with brisk capillary refill and an audible Doppler signal. Nerve function is intact. What is the next step?
o: Immediate open exploration of the brachial artery
Admit with the elbow in about 30–40° of flexion and monitor perfusion closely
Formal angiography before any further intervention
Remove the pins and immobilise in hyperflexion
items.e: A perfused (pink) but pulseless hand after satisfactory reduction is usually observed closely in hospital, as collateral flow is adequate; exploration is indicated if the hand becomes cold or white, perfusion worsens, or there is median nerve palsy or compartment syndrome.

items.q: An 8-year-old boy weighing 28 kg has a closed, length-stable transverse midshaft femoral fracture. The usual treatment of choice is:
o: Skin traction for 6 weeks followed by a cast
items.e: Flexible titanium elastic nails are the usual treatment for length-stable diaphyseal femoral fractures in children of about 5–11 years who weigh under about 45–50 kg; piriformis-entry rigid nails risk femoral head avascular necrosis in the skeletally immature, and spica casting is preferred under about 5 years.

items.q: A 58-year-old woman notices her foot flattening over a year. Viewed from behind, more lateral toes are visible on the affected side, and on single-limb heel rise the heel fails to invert and she cannot rise fully. The deformity corrects passively. Most likely diagnosis?
o: Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction (progressive collapsing foot deformity)
items.e: The 'too many toes' sign and failure of heel inversion on single heel rise in an adult with an acquired, flexible flatfoot are classic for posterior tibial tendon dysfunction; tarsal coalition causes a rigid flatfoot, usually presenting in adolescence.

items.q: A 15-year-old has a distal femoral metaphyseal lesion with a sunburst periosteal reaction, suspicious for osteosarcoma. Before biopsy, which investigation best defines local extent (marrow involvement, skip lesions, soft-tissue mass and neurovascular relations) for limb-salvage planning?
o: MRI of the entire femur including the adjacent joints
items.e: MRI of the whole involved bone defines intramedullary extent, skip metastases, soft-tissue extension and neurovascular involvement, and is ideally done before biopsy so post-biopsy oedema does not confound it; chest CT and bone scan or PET-CT stage distant disease.

items.q: A 5-year-old has a fever of 39.3 °C, a hot swollen left knee, pain on any passive movement, refuses to bear weight and has an ESR of 55 mm/h. Radiographs show only an effusion. What is the most important next investigation?
o: Joint aspiration for cell count, Gram stain and culture
items.e: Suspected septic arthritis needs urgent aspiration: synovial white cell count, Gram stain and culture confirm the diagnosis and guide antibiotics, and further imaging should not delay it; MRI is added if adjacent osteomyelitis is suspected.

items.q: In a zone II flexor digitorum profundus repair intended for early active motion, which factor contributes most to the tensile strength of the repair?
o: Placing the core suture purchase about 2 mm from the cut tendon ends
Relying on a running epitendinous suture alone
The number of core suture strands crossing the repair site
items.e: Repair strength rises roughly in proportion to the number of core strands crossing the repair, so 4- to 6-strand repairs are used to allow early active motion; thicker suture, core purchase of about 7–10 mm and an epitendinous suture add further strength.

items.q: A 12-year-old has an eccentric, expansile, lytic metaphyseal lesion of the proximal tibia. MRI shows multiple fluid–fluid levels separated by thin, smoothly enhancing septa with no solid or nodular enhancing component. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.e: Fluid–fluid levels with thin, uniformly enhancing septa and no solid component favour a primary aneurysmal bone cyst; thick nodular enhancing septa or a solid mass suggest telangiectatic osteosarcoma, and a simple bone cyst is central and usually has a single fluid level only after fracture.

items.q: A 24-year-old man has an isolated posterior wall fracture of the acetabulum after a dashboard injury; the hip is unstable on examination under anaesthesia. The surgical approach of choice for fixation is:
items.e: Posterior wall and posterior column fractures are reached through the Kocher–Langenbeck approach, which exposes the retroacetabular surface for lag-screw and buttress-plate fixation. The ilioinguinal, Stoppa and Smith-Petersen approaches give access to the anterior column and wall.

items.q: The Tubiana staging of Dupuytren disease is based on:
o: The number of digital rays involved
The thickness of the cord on ultrasound
The presence of ectopic deposits (knuckle pads, Ledderhose, Peyronie)
The total flexion deformity of the affected ray (MCP + PIP + DIP)
items.e: Tubiana stages each ray by the sum of the flexion deformities at the MCP, PIP and DIP joints (stage 1: 0–45°, 2: 45–90°, 3: 90–135°, 4: >135°). Ectopic deposits indicate Dupuytren diathesis but are not part of this staging.

items.q: In the combined task force (NASS/ASSR/ASNR) lumbar disc nomenclature, displaced disc material that has completely lost continuity with the parent disc is termed:
items.e: A sequestration is a subtype of extrusion in which the displaced fragment has no continuity with the disc of origin. In a protrusion the base is wider than the displaced material, while an extrusion has a narrower neck but remains attached; a bulge involves more than 25% of the disc circumference.

items.q: A 17-year-old has a permeative diaphyseal lesion of the femur with a large soft-tissue mass. Biopsy shows small round blue cells with membranous CD99 positivity and an EWSR1–FLI1 fusion. The standard systemic chemotherapy is:
o: Vincristine, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide (VDC/IE)
items.e: EWSR1–FLI1 [t(11;22)] with CD99 positivity confirms Ewing sarcoma, for which interval-compressed VDC alternating with IE is the standard regimen. MAP is used for osteosarcoma and imatinib for GIST and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

items.q: For staging a newly diagnosed high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma of the thigh, the investigation of choice to detect pulmonary metastases is:
items.e: The lung is the commonest site of metastasis from high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma, and CT of the chest is the standard staging test because it detects nodules too small for a chest radiograph. PET-CT is less sensitive than thin-section CT for small pulmonary nodules.

items.q: A 38-year-old man with chronic alcohol use has groin pain and normal hip radiographs. The most sensitive investigation to detect early osteonecrosis of the femoral head is:
items.e: MRI is the most sensitive and specific test for early (pre-collapse, Ficat I) osteonecrosis, showing a band-like lesion or the double-line sign before radiographs change. Bone scan is less sensitive and non-specific, and CT shows changes only later.

items.q: A 32-year-old has 3 months of back pain, night sweats and weight loss. MRI shows paradiscal involvement of T11–T12 with a subligamentous abscess spanning several levels; he is neurologically intact. Before starting definitive treatment, the most appropriate next step is:
o: Empirical antitubercular therapy for 12 months without tissue diagnosis
Anterior radical debridement and strut grafting
CT-guided biopsy for histopathology, culture and GeneXpert (CBNAAT)
items.e: Tissue diagnosis by image-guided biopsy confirms tuberculosis, excludes pyogenic infection and malignancy, and allows rapid detection of rifampicin resistance with GeneXpert, so the correct drug regimen can be chosen. Surgery is reserved for neurological deficit, instability, progressive kyphosis or failure of medical treatment.

items.q: The most common organism causing pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in adults is:
items.e: Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA) causes about half of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis. Gram-negative organisms such as E. coli follow urinary infection, and Pseudomonas is associated with intravenous drug use.

items.q: In supine hip arthroscopy, the anterior portal places which structure at greatest risk?
items.e: The anterior portal passes closest to the branches of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (within a few millimetres), and the femoral neurovascular bundle lies more medially. The anterolateral portal endangers the superior gluteal nerve and the posterolateral portal the sciatic nerve.

items.q: A 3-month-old girl has a dislocated hip that reduces with a clunk on the Ortolani manoeuvre. The most appropriate initial treatment is:
o: Observation with repeat ultrasound at 6 weeks
Closed reduction under anaesthesia and hip spica
Open reduction through a medial approach
items.e: A dislocated but reducible (Ortolani-positive) hip in an infant under 6 months is treated with a Pavlik harness, with ultrasound to confirm reduction. Closed reduction and spica is used if the harness fails or the child is older (about 6–18 months).

items.q: In the sample-size calculation for a randomised trial, the investigators set the power at 80%. Power is the probability of:
o: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true (type I error)
Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is false (type II error)
Correctly rejecting the null hypothesis when a true difference exists
Obtaining a p-value below 0.05 when the null hypothesis is true
items.e: Power equals 1 − β, the probability of detecting a true effect of the specified size. With 80% power there is a 20% chance of a type II error; α (usually 0.05) is the type I error rate.

items.q: In lamellar bone formation, hydroxyapatite crystals are first deposited mainly:
o: Within the cytoplasm of mature osteocytes
In the hole (gap) zones between staggered type I collagen molecules
By free precipitation in the interstitial fluid of the Haversian canal
Within proteoglycan aggregates of the cement line
items.e: Primary mineralisation of osteoid begins extracellularly, with calcium phosphate nucleating in the gap (hole) zones of the quarter-staggered type I collagen fibrils, aided by osteoblast-derived matrix vesicles. Crystals then grow along and between the fibrils during secondary mineralisation.

items.q: After successful Ponseti correction of idiopathic clubfoot, the most important risk factor for relapse is:
o: The number of casts needed to achieve correction
Incomplete correction of cavus in the first cast
Non-compliance with the foot abduction brace
items.e: Poor adherence to the foot abduction brace is the strongest and commonest cause of relapse after Ponseti treatment, increasing relapse risk several-fold. Tenotomy is a routine part of the method, and the number of casts is not a major independent predictor.

items.q: In the Gould modification of the Broström procedure for chronic lateral ankle instability, the anatomical repair of the ATFL and CFL is reinforced with the:
items.e: The modified Broström–Gould procedure imbricates the ATFL and CFL and advances the lateral limb of the inferior extensor retinaculum to the fibula, which reinforces the repair and limits subtalar inversion. Peroneus brevis is sacrificed in non-anatomical tenodeses such as Evans, Watson-Jones and Chrisman–Snook.

items.q: The characteristic biochemical change in the collagen of Dupuytren cords, compared with normal palmar fascia, is:
o: Replacement of type I collagen by type II collagen
An increased proportion of type III collagen relative to type I
Loss of all type I collagen
items.e: Normal palmar fascia is almost entirely type I collagen; in Dupuytren disease myofibroblasts lay down excess type III collagen, raising the type III:I ratio. Type II is cartilage collagen and type IV forms basement membranes.

items.q: On histology of a central cartilage tumour of the femur, which feature most reliably indicates an atypical cartilaginous tumour/grade 1 chondrosarcoma rather than an enchondroma?
o: Permeation of the medullary cavity with entrapment of host lamellar bone trabeculae
Encasement of cartilage lobules by a rim of lamellar bone
items.e: Infiltrative growth with permeation of marrow spaces and entrapment of pre-existing host trabeculae is the key histological criterion of malignancy in low-grade cartilage tumours. Enchondromas form discrete lobules encased by reactive lamellar bone, and cytological atypia alone is unreliable.

items.q: A 25-year-old has an upper trunk (C5–C6) brachial plexus avulsion with intact C7–T1 function, 3 months after injury. The standard nerve transfer to restore shoulder abduction and external rotation is:
o: Ulnar nerve fascicle to the biceps branch of the musculocutaneous nerve (Oberlin)
Spinal accessory nerve to the suprascapular nerve
Medial pectoral nerve to the musculocutaneous nerve
Anterior interosseous nerve to the ulnar motor branch
items.e: Transferring the distal spinal accessory nerve to the suprascapular nerve reinnervates supraspinatus and infraspinatus, often combined with a triceps branch to axillary nerve transfer for deltoid. The Oberlin transfer restores elbow flexion, not shoulder function.

items.q: In the Enneking (MSTS) surgical staging system for malignant bone tumours, stage III denotes:
o: A tumour of any grade or extent with regional or distant metastasis
A high-grade tumour with extracompartmental extension
A low-grade tumour with extracompartmental extension
A high-grade tumour confined to its compartment
items.e: Enneking stage III is defined by metastasis (M1), regardless of grade (G) or compartmental status (T). Stage I is low grade and stage II high grade, each subdivided into A (intracompartmental) and B (extracompartmental).
